source_text:
Πρόβατον ἤκουσεν· Ὡς γὰρ πρόβατον ἐπὶ σφαγὴν ἤχθη καὶ ὡς ἀμνὸς ἐναντίον τοῦ κείραντος
αὐτὸν ἄφωνος· πρόβατον ἤκουσεν διὰ τὴν σφαγὴν καὶ διὰ τὴν τῶν ἁγίων μελῶν αὐτοῦ μετάλημψιν καὶ τὴν ἐκ τῆς τοῦ ἁγίου αἵματος αὐτοῦ σφραγίδος ἀθάνατον αὐτοῦ φυλακήν. Ποιμὴν ἤκουσεν· Ἐγὼ γάρ εἰμι ὁ ποιμὴν ὁ καλός, ἐπειδὴ τὰ πεπλανημένα πρόβατα ἐπέστρεψεν καὶ τὸν ἀντίδικον ἡμῶν λέοντα τῇ βακτηρίᾳ τοῦ σταυροῦ ἀπέκτεινεν. Μαργαρίτης ἤκουσεν διὰ τὸ αὐτὸν ὥσπερ μαργαρίτην ἐν μύακι ἀνὰ μέσον δύο πτυχῶν σώματος καὶ ψυχῆς παρθενικῆς ἄνευ σπορᾶς ἀνδρὸς γεγεννῆσθαι ἢ διὰ τὸ εἶναι αὐτὸν κόσμιον ψυχῆς ἢ διὰ τὸ πολυφεγγὲς αὐτοῦ καὶ καθαρὸν καὶ πανταχόθεν τῇ αἴγλῃ τῆς θεότητος ἐξάστραπτον. Φῶς ἤκουσεν, ἦν γὰρ τὸ φῶς τὸ ἀληθινόν, ὃ φωτίζει πάντα ἄνθρωπον ἐρχόμενον εἰς τὸν κόσμον, ἐπειδὴ τὴν ζοφερὰν πλάνην τῆς παλαιᾶς σκοτομήνης ἀπὸ τῆς διανοίας ἡμῶν ἀπήλασεν καὶ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς τοῦ ἡγεμονικοῦ ἡμῶν νοῦ διήνοιξεν, ἵνα ἴδωμεν ἀληθῶς οἷς προσεκυνοῦμεν τὸ πρίν, ὅτι οὐκ εἰσὶ θεοί, ἀλλ' ἔργα χειρῶν ἀνθρώπων, λίθοι καὶ ξύλα. Λίθος ἀκρογωνιαῖος ἤκουσεν, ἐπειδὴ τοὺς δύο λαοὺς καθάπερ δύο τοίχους τῇ πίστει οἰκοδομήσας ἐπάνω αὐτῶν ἐπίκειται εἰς μίαν ἁρμογὴν σωτηρίας συνάγων. Ἥλιος δικαιοσύνης ἤκουσεν διὰ τὸ φωτεινὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ θερμόν –οὐκ ἔστιν γὰρ ὃς ἀποκρυβήσεται τὴν θέρμην αὐτοῦ, καὶ διὰ τὸ δωδεκάκτινον φῶς τῶν ἀποστόλων. Κόκκος σινάπεως ἤκουσεν, ἐπειδὴ σμικρύνει ἑαυτὸν καὶ συγκαταβαίνει ταῖς ἕξεσιν ἡμῶν παρὰ τὰς ἀρχὰς τῆς πίστεως, εἶθ' ὁπόταν εἰς τοὺς αὔλακας τῆς ψυχῆς ἡμῶν ἐμφωλεύσας εἰς βάθος διαχυθῇ, εἰς ὕψος οὐρανομῆκες ἐπαιρόμενος πρὸς εὐσέβειαν καὶ φρόνησιν ἀναθερμαίνεται. Σκώληξ ἤκουσεν· Ἐγὼ γάρ εἰμι σκώληξ καὶ οὐκ ἄνθρωπος, διὰ τὸ τὴν ἐξαστράπτουσαν θεότητα καθάπερ ἄγκιστρον τῷ σκώληκι τοῦ σώματος κρύψαντα αὐτὸν εἰς τόνδε τὸν βυθὸν τοῦ βίου χαλάσαντα καὶ ὥσπερ καλὸν ἁλιέα ἀνασπάσαντα πληρῶσαι τὸ γεγραμμένον· Ἄξεις δράκοντα ἐν ἀγκίστρῳ. Ἄνθρωπος ἤκουσεν, ἐπειδὴ σῶμα ἐφόρησεν οὐκ ἐξ ἡδονῆς καὶ ὕπνου συνεστώς, ἀλλ' ἐκ παρθένου καὶ πνεύματος ἁγίου γεγονώς. Ἀλλ' ἐπειδὴ ἕκαστος ἡμῶν, ἀγαπητοί, ἐκδέχεται καὶ τὴν τῶν πατέρων μελίρρυτον διδασκαλίαν, ἐνταῦθα τὸ βαλάντιον ἡμῶν τῶν λόγων σφραγισώμεθα ἁγίῳ πνεύματι, ἵνα αὐτοὶ ἐλθόντες ἐκ τῆς μελισταγοῦς σοφίας τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τὰς δεξαμενὰς τῶν καρδιῶν ἡμῶν πληρώσωσιν, καὶ πολὺν τὸν καρπὸν τῆς εὐσεβείας ἕκαστος ὑμῶν βλαστήσῃ καὶ ὁ μὲν ποιήσῃ τριάκοντα, ὁ δὲ ἑξήκοντα, ὁ δὲ ἑκατὸν τὸν στέφανον τῶν ἀγγέλων, ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τῷ κυρίῳ ἡμῶν, μεθ' οὗ τῷ πατρὶ δόξα, τιμή, κράτος ἅμα τῷ ἁγίῳ καὶ ζωοποιῷ πνεύματι, νῦν καὶ εἰς τοὺς σύμπαντας αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν.
thought_title: The many names of Christ and their works, closed with a doxology
orientation: Amphilochius is finishing his list of Christ's names, explaining each name by a work of Christ, and then he closes the homily by deferring to the fathers' teaching and blessing the congregation.
pass_a_gloss: He was called sheep: For as a sheep he was led to slaughter and as a lamb before the one shearing it voiceless; he was called sheep because of the slaughter and because of the partaking of his holy members and the immortal guarding of him from the seal of his holy blood. He was called shepherd: For I am the good shepherd, since he turned back the wandering sheep and killed our adversary the lion with the staff of the cross. He was called pearl because he was born just as a pearl in an oyster between two folds of a virginal body and soul without seed of a man, or because he is an ornament of the soul, or because of his many-shining and pure and from every side flashing with the radiance of the Godhead. He was called light, for he was the true light, which enlightens every man coming into the world, since he drove away the dark error of the old darkness from our mind and opened the eyes of our ruling intellect, so that we may see truly that the things which we formerly worshipped are not gods, but works of human hands, stones and wood. He was called cornerstone, since having built the two peoples just as two walls by faith he lies upon them, gathering them into one joining of salvation. He was called sun of righteousness because of his shining and warmth—for there is no one who will be hidden from his warmth—and because of the twelve-rayed light of the apostles. He was called mustard seed, since he makes himself small and comes down to our conditions at the beginnings of faith, then whenever having nested in the furrows of our soul he is poured out into depth, being lifted to a heaven-high height he is warmed toward piety and wisdom. He was called worm: For I am a worm and not a man, because having hidden the flashing Godhead just as a hook in the worm of the body, having let himself down into this deep of life and having drawn up just as a good fisherman, to fulfill what is written: You will lead the dragon with a hook. He was called man, since he wore a body not composed from pleasure and sleep, but having come into being from a virgin and the Holy Spirit. But since each of us, beloved, awaits also the honey-flowing teaching of the fathers, here let us seal our purse of words with the Holy Spirit, so that they themselves coming from the honey-dripping wisdom of our Lord Jesus Christ may fill the cisterns of our hearts, and each of you may sprout much fruit of piety, and one may produce thirty, another sixty, another a hundred the crown of the angels, in Christ Jesus our Lord, with whom to the Father be glory, honor, might together with the Holy and life-giving Spirit, now and unto all the ages of ages. Amen.

choices.why: Glossary requires 'sheep' for πρόβατον, not 'lamb'; the source distinguishes πρόβατον from ἀμνός (lamb) in the Isaiah quotation.
Glossary requires 'sun of righteousness' for ἥλιος δικαιοσύνης.
Glossary requires 'mustard seed' for κόκκος σινάπεως.

pass_b_english: He was called sheep: For he was led like a sheep to the slaughter, and like a lamb silent before its shearer (Isaiah 53:7). He was called sheep because of the slaughter, and because of the partaking of his holy members, and because of the immortal protection that comes from the seal of his holy blood. He was called shepherd: For I am the good shepherd (John 10:11), because he turned back the sheep that had gone astray and killed the lion who opposes us with the staff of the cross. He was called pearl because, like a pearl in an oyster between two folds, he was born from a virgin without the seed of a man, or because he is the adornment of the soul, or because of his many-shining, pure radiance flashing everywhere with the brightness of divinity. He was called light—for he was the true light, which enlightens every person coming into the world (John 1:9), because he drove the dark error of the old gloom from our minds and opened the eyes of our ruling intellect, so that we might truly see that the things we once worshiped are not gods but works of human hands, stones and wood. He was called cornerstone because, having built the two peoples like two walls by faith, he rests upon them, gathering them into one bond of salvation. He was called sun of righteousness because of his brightness and warmth—for there is nothing hidden from his heat—and because of the twelve-rayed light of the apostles. He was called mustard seed because he makes himself small and comes down to our capacities at the beginnings of faith; then, when he has nestled into the furrows of our soul and spread into its depths, it rises to a heaven-high height and is kindled toward piety and wisdom. He was called worm: For I am a worm and not a man, because he hid his flashing divinity like a hook in the worm of his body, let himself down into this deep of life, and like a good fisherman drew up his catch, fulfilling what was written: You will draw the dragon with a hook. He was called man because he wore a body not composed from pleasure and sleep, but having come to be from a virgin and the Holy Spirit. But since each of us, beloved, receives also the honey-flowing teaching of the fathers, let us seal here the purse of our words with the Holy Spirit, so that when they come from the honey-dripping wisdom of our Lord Jesus Christ they may fill the cisterns of our hearts, and each of you may sprout much fruit of piety—one producing thirty, another sixty, another a hundred, the crown of the angels—in Christ Jesus our Lord, with whom to the Father be glory, honor, and might, together with the holy and life-giving Spirit, now and to all the ages of ages. Amen.

problems.quote: He was called worm: For I am a worm and not a man (Psalm 22:6), because he hid his flashing divinity like a hook in the worm of his body, let himself down into this deep of life, and like a good fisherman drew up what was written: You will draw the dragon with a hook (Job 41:1).
problems.source_quote: Σκώληξ ἤκουσεν· Ἐγὼ γάρ εἰμι σκώληξ καὶ οὐκ ἄνθρωπος, ... Ἄξεις δράκοντα ἐν ἀγκίστρῳ.
problems.why: The source does not cite Psalm 22:6 nor Job 41:1; both citations are unwarranted additions.
problems.fix: He was called worm: For I am a worm and not a man, because he hid his flashing divinity like a hook in the worm of his body, let himself down into this deep of life, and like a good fisherman drew up what was written: You will draw the dragon with a hook.

problems.quote: You will draw the dragon with a hook (Job 41:1).
problems.source_quote: Ἄξεις δράκοντα ἐν ἀγκίστρῳ.
problems.why: The source contains the phrase but does not attribute it to Job 41:1; the citation is an unwarranted addition.
problems.fix: You will draw the dragon with a hook.

problems.quote: You will draw the dragon with a hook (Job 41:1)
problems.source_quote: Ἄξεις δράκοντα ἐν ἀγκίστρῳ
problems.why: The source quotes Ἄξεις δράκοντα ἐν ἀγκίστρῳ, which is LXX Job 40:20 (Hebrew 41:1). The English gives 'Job 41:1' which follows Hebrew numbering, but the work brief states 'Citations should be given in modern form with LXX Psalm numbering noted where it differs from the Hebrew.' For Job, the LXX numbering differs: LXX Job 40:20 = Hebrew Job 41:1. The English gives Hebrew numbering without noting LXX difference.
problems.fix: You will draw the dragon with a hook (Job 40:20 LXX / 41:1 Heb.)
problems.ruling: Cites Hebrew Job 41:1 but source is LXX Job 40:20; brief requires LXX numbering.

problems.quote: like a pearl in an oyster between two shells, he was born between body and soul of a virgin
problems.source_quote: ὥσπερ μαργαρίτην ἐν μύακι ἀνὰ μέσον δύο πτυχῶν σώματος καὶ ψυχῆς παρθενικῆς ἄνευ σπορᾶς ἀνδρὸς γεγεννῆσθαι
problems.why: The Greek says 'born from a virgin without man's seed,' with 'between two folds of body and soul of a virgin' describing the μύαξ/oyster context. The English 'born between body and soul of a virgin' makes it sound like Christ was born between Mary's body and soul, rather than 'from a virgin' being the birth and 'between two folds' describing the pearl/oyster analogy.
problems.fix: like a pearl in an oyster between two folds, he was born from a virgin without the seed of a man
problems.ruling: Greek says born from a virgin; English implies born between body and soul, mis‑rendering the analogy.

problems.quote: he rests upon them, joining them into one fitting of salvation
problems.source_quote: ἐπάνω αὐτῶν ἐπίκειται εἰς μίαν ἁρμογὴν σωτηρίας συνάγων
problems.why: 'one fitting of salvation' is awkward. ἁρμογή means 'joining, joint, union.' The English 'one fitting of salvation' is unclear; better 'one joint/union of salvation.'
problems.fix: he rests upon them, gathering them into one bond of salvation
problems.ruling: ἁρμογὴ means union/joint; "one fitting" is obscure and mis‑captures the sense of a single union of salvation.

problems.quote: he rises to a height reaching heaven
problems.source_quote: εἰς ὕψος οὐρανομῆκες ἐπαιρόμενος
problems.why: Same issue: subject should be 'it' (the seed/faith), not 'he.'
problems.fix: it rises to a heaven-high height
problems.ruling: Greek subject is the seed/faith; English uses "he", mis‑identifying the referent.

problems.quote: and grows warm toward piety and wisdom
problems.source_quote: πρὸς εὐσέβειαν καὶ φρόνησιν ἀναθερμαίνεται
problems.why: Same subject issue: 'it grows warm,' not 'he.'
problems.fix: and is kindled toward piety and wisdom
problems.ruling: Same pronoun error as #6; subject should be the seed, not "he".

fixed: Removed unwarranted Psalm 22:6 and Job 41:1 citations from the worm passage; source has no such citations.
Corrected 'born between body and soul of a virgin' to 'born from a virgin without the seed of a man'; source: παρθενικῆς ἄνευ σπορᾶς ἀνδρὸς γεγεννῆσθαι.
Changed 'one fitting of salvation' to 'one bond of salvation'; source: μίαν ἁρμογὴν σωτηρίας.
Changed subject from 'he' to 'it' for the mustard seed and adjusted 'grows warm' to 'is kindled'; source: ἐπαιρόμενος ... ἀναθερμαίνεται referring to the seed.

problems.quote: He was called pearl because, like a pearl in an oyster between two folds, he was born from a virgin without the seed of a man without the seed of a man, or because he is the adornment of the soul, or because of his many-shining, pure radiance flashing everywhere with the brightness of divinity.
problems.source_quote: Μαργαρίτης ἤκουσεν διὰ τὸ αὐτὸν ὥσπερ μαργαρίτην ἐν μύακι ἀνὰ μέσον δύο πτυχῶν σώματος καὶ ψυχῆς παρθενικῆς ἄνευ σπορᾶς ἀνδρὸς γεγεννῆσθαι ἢ διὰ τὸ εἶναι αὐτὸν κόσμιον ψυχῆς ἢ διὰ τὸ πολυφεγγὲς αὐτοῦ καὶ καθαρὸν καὶ πανταχόθεν τῇ αἴγλῃ τῆς θεότητος ἐξάστραπτον.
problems.why: The Greek personifies the pearl speaking; the English changes this to ‘He was called pearl’, misrepresenting the speaker.
problems.fix: Pearl said: “I am like a pearl in an oyster between two folds, born of a virgin without a man’s seed, or I am the adornment of the soul, or I shine with the pure radiance of divinity.”

problems.quote: He was called worm: For I am a worm and not a man, because he hid his flashing divinity like a hook in the worm of his body, let himself down into this deep of life, and like a good fisherman drew up what was written: You will draw the dragon with a hook.
problems.source_quote: Σκώληξ ἤκουσεν· Ἐγὼ γάρ εἰμι σκώληξ καὶ οὐκ ἄνθρωπος, διὰ τὸ τὴν ἐξαστράπτουσαν θεότητα καθάπερ ἄγκιστρον τῷ σκώληκι τοῦ σώματος κρύψαντα αὐτὸν εἰς τὸν βυθὸν τοῦ βίου χαλάσαντα καὶ ὥσπερ καλὸν ἁλιέα ἀνασπάσαντα πληρῶσαι τὸ γεγραμμένον· Ἄξεις δράκοντα ἐν ἀγκίστρῳ.
problems.why: The source presents Worm speaking; the English changes it to a label, altering agency and adding “He was called”.
problems.fix: Worm said: “I am a worm and not a man; I hide my flashing divinity like a hook in the worm of my body, descend into the deep of life, and, like a good fisherman, draw up what is written: ‘You will draw the dragon with a hook.’”

problems.quote: He was called man because he wore a body not composed from pleasure and sleep, but made from a virgin and the Holy Spirit.
problems.source_quote: Ἀνθρωπος ἤκουσεν, ἐπειδά σῶμα ἐφόρησεν οὐκ ἐξ ἡδονῆς καὶ ὕπνου συνεστώς, ἀλλ' ἐκ παρθένου καὶ πνεύματος ἁγίου γεγονώς.
problems.why: The Greek personifies Man speaking; the English recasts it as a title, changing who is speaking.
problems.fix: Man said: “I bore a body not from pleasure and sleep, but from a virgin and the Holy Spirit.”

problems.quote: (Psalm 19:6)
problems.source_quote: οὐκ ἔστιν γὰρ ὃς ἀποκρυβήσεται τὴν θέρμην αὐτοῦ
problems.why: Wrong citation: The quote matches Psalm 18:7 LXX (Psalm 19:6 Hebrew is different wording).
problems.fix: (Psalm 18:7 LXX)
problems.ruling: Citation mismatches; phrase belongs to Psalm 18 LXX, not Psalm 19:6

problems.quote: He was called sheep: For he was led like a sheep to the slaughter, and like a lamb silent before its shearer (Isaiah 53:7).
problems.source_quote: Πρόβατον ἤκουσεν· Ὡς γὰρ πρόβατον ἐπὶ σφαγὴν ἤχθη καὶ ὡς ἀμνὸς ἐναντίον τοῦ κείραντος αὐτὸν ἄφωνος
problems.why: The Greek says ‘Sheep heard…’, i.e., the personified sheep speaks; the English rewrites it as ‘He was called sheep’, changing the speaker.
problems.fix: Sheep said: “For as a sheep I was led to slaughter and as a lamb before the shearer I was silent.”
problems.ruling: Greek ἤκουσεν means 'was heard' (passive), not 'heard' (active); personification lost.

problems.quote: He was called shepherd: For I am the good shepherd (John 10:11), because he turned back the sheep that had gone astray and killed the lion who opposes us with the staff of the cross.
problems.source_quote: Ποιμὴν ἤκουσεν· Ἐγὼ γάρ εἰμι ὁ ποιμὴν ὁ καλός, ἐπειδά τὰ πεπλανημένα πρόβατα ἐπέστρεψεν καὶ τὸν ἀντίδικον ἡμῶν λέοντα τῇ βακτηρίᾳ τοῦ σταυροῦ ἀπέκτεινεν.
problems.why: The source has the shepherd speaking; the English presents it as a label ‘He was called shepherd’, altering who is speaking.
problems.fix: Shepherd said: “I am the good shepherd, for I have turned back the wandering sheep and killed the lion that opposes us with the power of the cross.”
problems.ruling: Same pattern: Ποιμὴν ἤκουσεν = 'Shepherd was heard,' personified voice erased.

problems.quote: He was called light—for he was the true light, which enlightens every person coming into the world (John 1:9)—because he drove the dark error of the old gloom from our minds and opened the eyes of our ruling intellect, so that we might truly see that the things we once worshiped are not gods but works of human hands, stones and wood.
problems.source_quote: Φῶς ἤκουσεν, ἦν γὰρ τὸ φῶς τὸ ἀληθινόν, ὃ φωτίζει πάντα ἄνθρωπον ἐρχόμενον εἰς τὸν κόσμον, ἐπειδύτὴν τὴν ζοφερὰν πλάνην τῆς παλαιᾶς σκοτομήνης ἀπὸ τῆς διανοίας ἡμῶν ἀπήλασεν καὶ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς τοῦ ἡγεμονικοῦ ἡμῶν νοῦ διήνοιξεν, ἵνα ὴδωμεν ἀληθῶς οἷς προσεκυνοῦμεν τὸ πρίν, ὅτι οὐκ εἰσὶ θεοί, ἀλλ' ἔργα χειρῶν ἀνθρώπων, λίθοι καὶ ξύλα.
problems.why: The source has Light speaking; the English recasts it as a title, losing the personified voice.
problems.fix: Light said: “I am the true light that enlightens every person coming into the world, for I have removed the dark error of old gloom from our minds and opened the eyes of our governing intellect, so that we may truly see that those we once worshipped are not gods but works of human hands, stones and wood.”
problems.ruling: Φῶς ἤκουσεν = 'Light was heard,' not 'He was called light'; personification removed.

problems.quote: He was called cornerstone because, having built the two peoples like two walls by faith, he rests upon them, gathering them into one bond of salvation.
problems.source_quote: Λίθος ἀκρογωνιαῖος ἤκουσεν, ἐπειδή τοὺς δύο λαοὺς καθάπερ δύο τοίχους τῇ πίστει οἰκοδομήσας ἐπάνω αὐτῶν ἐπίκειται εἰς μίαν ἁρμογὴν σωτηρίας συνάγων.
problems.why: The Greek has Cornerstone speaking; the English changes it to a label, altering agency.
problems.fix: Cornerstone said: “Having built the two peoples like two walls by faith, I rest upon them, joining them into one bond of salvation.”
problems.ruling: Λίθος ἀκρογωνιαῖος ἤκουσεν = 'Cornerstone was heard,' voice changed to label.

problems.quote: He was called sun of righteousness because of his brightness and warmth—for there is nothing hidden from his heat (Psalm 19:6)—and because of the twelve-rayed light of the apostles.
problems.source_quote: Ἥλιος δικαιοσύνης ἤκουσεν διὰ τὸ φωτεινὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ θερμόν –οὐκ ἔστιν γὰρ ὃς ἀποκρυβήσεται τὴν θέρμην αὐτοῦ, καὶ διὰ τὸ δωδεκάκτινον φῶς τῶν ἀποστόλων.
problems.why: Again the personified Sun is turned into a title ‘He was called sun of righteousness’, changing the speaker.
problems.fix: Sun of righteousness said: “Because of my bright and warm light—nothing can hide from my heat—and because of the twelve‑rayed light of the apostles.”
problems.ruling: Ἥλιος δικαιοσύνης ἤκουσεν = 'Sun of righteousness was heard,' agency lost.

problems.quote: Sheep said: For I was led like a sheep to the slaughter
problems.source_quote: Πρόβατον ἤκουσεν· Ὡς γὰρ πρόβατον ἐπὶ σφαγὴν ἤχθη
problems.why: Source has passive 'was heard/called' not active 'said'; Christ is spoken about, not speaking.
problems.fix: He was called sheep: for he was led like a sheep to the slaughter
problems.ruling: Greek ἤκουσεν = heard, not said; English uses first‑person speech

problems.quote: Shepherd said: I am the good shepherd
problems.source_quote: Ποιμὴν ἤκουσεν· Ἐγὼ γάρ εἰμι ὁ ποιμὴν ὁ καλός

problems.quote: I rest upon them, gathering them into one bond of salvation
problems.source_quote: ἐπάνω αὐτῶν ἐπίκειται εἰς μίαν ἁρμογὴν σωτηρίας συνάγων
problems.why: Source says 'he rests upon them' not 'I rest'; third person throughout.

problems.quote: Because of my brightness and warmth

problems.quote: for there is nothing hidden from my heat

problems.quote: let myself down into this deep of life
problems.source_quote: αὐτὸν εἰς τόνδε τὸν βυθὸν τοῦ βίου χαλάσαντα

problems.quote: I wore a body not composed from pleasure and sleep

problems.quote: Sheep said:

problems.why: Greek says the sheep heard, not that it spoke.
problems.fix: Sheep heard:

fixed: Changed 'Sheep said' to 'He was called sheep' and adjusted pronouns to third person, matching Πρόβατον ἤκουσεν and Ὡς γὰρ πρόβατον ἐπὶ σφαγὴν ἤχθη.
Changed 'Shepherd said' to 'He was called shepherd' and adjusted 'I turned back' to 'he turned back', matching Ποιμὴν ἤκουσεν and ἐπέστρεψεν.
Changed 'Pearl said' to 'He was called pearl because' and adjusted pronouns to third person, matching Μαργαρίτης ἤκουσεν διὰ τὸ αὐτὸν.
Changed 'Light said' to 'He was called light—for he was' and adjusted pronouns to third person, matching Φῶς ἤκουσεν, ἦν γὰρ τὸ φῶς.
Changed 'Cornerstone said' to 'He was called cornerstone because' and adjusted 'I rest' to 'he rests', matching Λίθος ἀκρογωνιαῖος ἤκουσεν and ἐπίκειται.
Changed 'Sun of righteousness said' to 'He was called sun of righteousness because' and adjusted 'my' to 'his', matching Ἥλιος δικαιοσύνης ἤκουσεν διὰ τὸ φωτεινὸν αὐτοῦ.

Changed 'Worm said' to 'He was called worm' and adjusted 'I hid' to 'he hid', 'my body' to 'his body', and 'let myself down' to 'let himself down', matching Σκώληξ ἤκουσεν and the third-person participles.
Changed 'Man said' to 'He was called man because' and adjusted 'I wore' to 'he wore', matching Ἄνθρωπος ἤκουσεν, ἐπειδὴ σῶμα ἐφόρησεν.
Changed 'is waiting also for' to 'receives also', matching ἐκδέχεται.
Removed the incorrect Psalm citation 'Psalm 18:7 LXX' because the quoted Greek does not correspond to that verse; the source does not provide a precise citation.
Left 'flashing divinity' unchanged: the Greek ἐξαστράπτουσαν means 'flashing' or 'shining brightly', not 'extinguishing'.

fixed.fix: drew up his catch, fulfilling what was written
fixed.note: In the Greek he draws up the catch and so fulfils Scripture; the English makes "what was written" the thing drawn up.

dismissed.quote: like a hook in the worm of his body
dismissed.why: Greek has 'like a hook to/for the worm of the body' (dative), meaning divinity is the hook, body is the worm/bait. English 'in the worm' makes divinity located inside the worm, reversing the metaphor. The hook (divinity) is attached to the worm (body), not hidden inside it.
dismissed.note: With κρύψαντα the dative means "hid in the worm of his body", so the English is right and "to the worm" would be worse.

dismissed.quote: like a good fisherman drew up
dismissed.why: Greek has 'like a good fisherman, drawing up'—the participle ἀνασπάσαντα agrees with the subject (Christ). English 'like a good fisherman drew up' makes 'fisherman' the subject of 'drew up,' but Christ is the one who draws up, acting as/like a fisherman.
dismissed.note: "Like a good fisherman drew up" already makes Christ the subject; the fix to the overlapping text belongs to finding #1.
